speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to your consultation. I will be asking you a series of questions to understand your chronic joint pain, so I need to know: which specific joints are affected, how long have you been experiencing these symptoms, and does the pain worsen with activity or improve with rest?

speaker: Patient
text: 69-year-old male. The patient presents with pain in his left great toe, hips, and knees that worsens with activity and improves with rest. He reports that the symptoms have progressively gotten worse over the past several years.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is helpful; the pattern of pain worsening with activity and improving with rest often suggests osteoarthritis. However, given the involvement of your great toe alongside the hips and knees, I need to rule out gout and other inflammatory conditions. Did you notice any sudden, severe flares of redness and swelling, particularly in your toe, or do you have a history of high blood pressure?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain in the left great toe, hips, and knees. I also have Symptoms worsen with activity, Symptoms improve with rest.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Osteoarthritis. While your history of pain in the left great toe could suggest gout or psoriatic arthritis, the progressive nature of your symptoms over several years and the classic pattern of pain worsening with activity and improving with rest are highly characteristic of osteoarthritis. No further testing is required at this time.
